title: Vilnius → Tallinn → ferry → Tampere
meta: 04:00 start · 780 km · 10 h door to door

callout.html: **The hard day.** 600 km to Tallinn, a ferry, then 180 km more. It works only if you leave at 04:00 and stop four times. The baby will sleep through the first three hours — use them.

items.h: Load the car in the dark
items.p: Bags packed the night before, thermos filled, children carried out in pyjamas. Check passports, car documents, and that the ferry booking is on a phone that will not die.
170 km of empty road. **Nobody talks.** The 9- and 7-year-old will sleep; the baby will sleep if the car is warm and moving.
Fuel, toilets, first nappy. Ten minutes maximum: the trick on this drive is short stops, not long ones.
Another 130 km. Breakfast from the bag: rye bread, cheese, bananas, a flask of coffee. Do not sit down in a café — it costs an hour.
Fuel and coffee at the bypass, no city entry. This is where you realise the trip is really happening.
130 km, the prettiest stretch: forest, bog, the first sea light.
Twenty minutes by the beach if it is not raining, otherwise a petrol-station coffee. Legs out, baby fed, everyone back in.
130 km. The children will ask 'are we there yet' exactly here.
Tallink check-in. Be at the gate **45 minutes before** departure with a car — the queue closes 30 minutes before. Have the booking reference ready.
Tallinn 13:30 → Helsinki 15:30. Eat on board: the buffet is expensive, the café deck is fine. There is a play area and a deck to stand on. **This is the baby's best nap of the day.**
180 km of motorway, 1 h 50. Last stop at a ABC/Neste station before Tampere for milk, bread and breakfast — **most Finnish shops are shut on All Saints' Day.**
Keys, lift, bags. The flat is 2 km west of the centre on the lake. Do not unpack properly tonight.
Either **[[kaisla]]** (12 min walk along the water) or **[[hesburger]]** on Keskustori if everyone is finished. No cooking tonight.
If the flat has a sauna, use it after the children are down. Finnish apartments usually do — and it is the fastest way to feel human again.

alts: **Running late at Tallinn?** The 16:30 Megastar is the safety net — you reach Tampere around 20:30. Do not try to catch a ferry you cannot make; the ticket can be changed for a fee.
**Ferry choice:** the 12:30 Victoria I takes 3.5 h instead of 2 h but gives you a proper sit-down meal and more space. With a 9-month-old, that is sometimes the better trade.
**Driving at night:** do not. The last 180 km in Finland are moose country after dark and the children will not sleep twice.
note: Book the ferry before you leave Vilnius. A car with five people on a Saturday in winter is not a walk-up purchase, and the cheap fares are the early bookings.

title: All Saints' Day: tower, Moomin, candles
meta: Dry · 7 °C · sunset 16:22 · the gentlest day of the week

callout.html: **No driving today.** Everything is within 3 km of the flat. Finland is quiet — All Saints' is a family day, not a shopping day, and the evening belongs to candles.

items.p: You bought bread last night. Nobody leaves the flat before 09:45 — the children need a slow morning after 780 km.
Twenty minutes' drive, or a 35-minute walk. Climb the 130 steps (€2 adult, €1 child), then eat warm cardamom doughnuts at the café below. **The single best-value hour in Tampere.**
Pyynikki is the world's largest gravel ridge. A flat 1 km path through pine trees, then back to the car. The baby can sleep in the buggy here — it is the one place the wheels work.
**The market hall is closed.** Use **[[pancho]]** on Hämeenkatu (children's menu, crayons) or **[[napoli]]** for a big pizza to share. Both are 5 minutes from the cathedral.
Granite, 1907, and the strangest frescoes in Finland. Free. Let the 9-year-old find the skeletons carrying flowers.
Sunday hours 9–17. Family ticket €36 covers all five, and the Studio workshop (12:00–16:00) is included — glue, paper, and three children sitting still.

Sunset is 16:22. On All Saints' weekend Finnish families light candles on every grave; the whole hillside is a field of small flames. Free, silent, unforgettable. **Explain it to the children first, quietly.**
Dark at 16:30, so the evening is indoors. Cook, sauna, and get everyone to bed by 20:30 — tomorrow is a moving day.

alts: **Rain?** Swap the tower for the Moomin Museum in the morning and the swimming hall in the afternoon.
**Children with energy to burn:** [[koskipuisto]] playground by the rapids, 10 minutes from the cathedral, free.
**Want the forest instead?** [[kintulammi]] — a fire, sausages, 25 minutes north. Only if you are all awake by 09:00.
note: All Saints' Day is 31 Oct in Finland, but the candles stay lit all weekend. Sunday evening is the quietest and most beautiful.

title: Check out, swim, move to the second flat
meta: 3.7 mm rain · the wettest day · museums closed

callout.html: **Every museum in Tampere is closed on Monday** — Vapriikki, the Moomin Museum, Milavida. This is the day to swim, eat mustamakkara and move house.

items.p: The market is busiest 8–12. Buy sausage by weight at Tapola, add lingonberry jam, drink milk from a paper cup. About €12 for all five, eaten standing up.
Open Monday 9–18. Rye bread, cheese, pastries, fruit for the new flat. This is also the cheapest lunch in the centre if you are hungry again.
Checkout is usually 11:00–12:00. Strip the beds, empty the fridge, put everything in the boot. Leave the buggy out.
Kaleva, open Monday, warm children's pool. Two hours of guaranteed happiness on the wettest day of the week, about €22 for five. Bring towels and a padlock.
Ten minutes across town. Unpack properly this time — you are here for five nights, and the work week starts tomorrow.
[[kcitymarket]] in Lielahti is open until 22:00. Buy for three breakfasts and two dinners. This is where the food budget is won.
Pasta or soup at home. Tomorrow the alarm is for work, not for children.

alts: **Still in the first flat?** You can stay until checkout, leave bags, swim, and move in the afternoon. Ask the host for a 12:00 checkout when you book.
**Awful weather and no energy:** [[ratina]] mall — heated, food court, cinema, supermarket, bus station. Not glamorous, entirely practical.
note: Book the second flat for 2–7 Nov (5 nights) as soon as you can. Tampere fills up in early November with conferences, and a family of five needs parking plus a lift.

title: Dad works · family takes Vapriikki

callout.html: **First solo day for mum.** The rule for this week: one indoor anchor, one short walk, home before dark. Everything below is doable with three children and no second adult.

items.p: The flat has the kitchen table; the [[library_uni]] is the quiet alternative, 12 minutes' walk, free, with guest wifi.
Ten museums, one ticket, €38 for the family. Dinosaurs, the Hockey Hall of Fame, minerals that glow. Warm, with lifts and toilets on every floor.
The museum restaurant: a lunch plate, salad bar and a children's portion. You do not have to put coats back on, which is the whole point.
Free, warm, ten minutes' walk. A whole floor of children's books, a baby-changing room, and sofas. The 7-year-old reads; the baby crawls.
Sunset 16:17. Walk back along the rapids, or take the bus. Home for milk and a nap for whoever still naps.
Cook at home. If everyone needs to get out, [[plevna]] in the Finlayson mill takes five without a booking at 17:00.

alts: **Museum fatigue?** Swap Vapriikki for [[tallipiha]] (free, chocolate, glassblowing) plus the Finlayson courtyard.
**The 9-month-old is done by 11:00:** go to Vapriikki at 10:00 sharp, leave at 12:00, and skip the library.
note: One adult, three children, short days. Two hours out, one hour home is a good day — do not try to fill eight hours.

title: Hämeenlinna: a real castle

callout.html: **The best day trip of the week.** 79 km each way on a motorway, a medieval castle, and a park with a tower. Leave by 09:00 — the castle shuts at 16:00 and the light goes at 16:14.

items.p: 79 km, one hour. Motorway the whole way; the baby will sleep. Park at the castle car park.
A 13th-century brick castle on the lake. Ramparts, a great hall, a tower to climb, model knights. Family ticket about €35. **Carrier, not buggy.**
The castle café is small. The town centre is 800 m: pizza, soup or a market lunch for about €40 for five.
Ten minutes away: a 19th-century landscape park of ridges and ponds, with a tower (€2) over Lake Vanajavesi. Free to walk, flat paths, no traffic.
Home by 15:45, before dark. The children will sleep in the car — carry them in.
Dad finishes work. Soup, bath, early night.

alts: **Castle closed or too much?** Hämeenlinna has a prison museum and a glass museum, but honestly: skip the second sight and go home.
**Raining hard:** turn around and go to [[ideapark]] instead — 20 minutes, indoors, no castles.
note: Häme Castle is closed on Mondays and shuts at 16:00 Tue–Fri. Check the day before; Finnish winter hours are unforgiving.

title: Kangasala: old cars in a pine forest
meta: 0 mm · 7 °C · gusts 55 km/h — a windy, dry day

callout.html: **Short drive, free museum, big view.** Twenty-five minutes each way, so even a bad night with the baby does not ruin it. If the wind is as strong as forecast, skip the ridge and stay in the museum café.

items.p: 25 km, 30 minutes. The road runs between lakes the whole way.
A volunteer-run museum of Finnish motoring: 1930s saloons, motorcycles, engines, all in a lakeside pine park. **Free** (donation). Warm and small enough for a 9-month-old.
Fifteen minutes away: a short steep climb to the view that a Finnish painter made famous in 1858, with a wooden café pavilion. Free. **Carrier, not buggy.**
The pavilion café does soup and pulla; the town centre has a pizzeria. About €35 for five.
Home by 15:00, before the light goes.
Friday is the last Tampere day; Saturday is Helsinki and the ferry. Start the laundry tonight.

alts: **Too windy for the ridge:** the museum café has a view of its own. Or drive to [[ideapark]] on the way home.
**Children want water:** [[pyynikin_uimahalli]] is 15 minutes from home and warm.
note: Vehoniemi's winter hours are shorter than summer — check the website the night before. If it is shut, the ridge and the café still make the drive worth it.

title: Last Tampere day: free museum, pack the car

callout.html: **Vapriikki is free for everyone on Fridays 15:00–18:00.** If you skipped it on Tuesday, this is the day. If you did not, come back for the halls you missed and save €38.

items.p: Five nights in one flat means one laundry day. Start it now, not tomorrow morning.
The old stable yards: chocolate shop, glassblower, toy shop, café, cobbles. Free, compact, no traffic. The 7-year-old will watch the glass for ten minutes.
Brewery restaurant in the mill next door: sausages, schnitzel, children's portions, big tables. Book for five at 12:30 or just walk in early.
Fridays 15:00–18:00, no ticket. Do the halls you missed, or let the children go straight back to the dinosaurs.
One bag per person plus a bag for the ferry. Sausages and matches out of the boot. Charge everything.
Something easy and early — [[sitko]] pizza or leftovers. Tomorrow starts at 08:30.

alts: **Want one more forest?** [[niihama]] café and the Kauppi trails, 15 minutes north, if it is dry.
**Want one more swim?** [[pyynikin_uimahalli]] in the morning instead of Tallipiha.
note: Check out on Saturday morning is usually 11:00, but you are leaving at 08:30 — tell the host the night before and leave the keys as agreed.

title: Tampere → Heureka → ferry → Tallinn
meta: 0.6 mm · 6 °C · the long transit day, west to east

callout.html: **Two borders, one museum, one ferry.** Leave Tampere by 08:30. Heureka is 15 minutes off the motorway and worth three hours; the ferry check-in closes 45 minutes before sailing.

items.p: 165 km to Vantaa, 1 h 45. Breakfast in the car; the children sleep the first hour.
Buy tickets online the night before: €23 adult / €16 child instead of €26/€19, and under-5s free. Everything can be touched. Three hours disappears.
The science restaurant does a family lunch, or eat the sandwiches you brought in the picnic room downstairs.
25 km, 30 minutes, through Vantaa and Helsinki. Fill the car before the ferry — Finnish fuel is cheaper than Estonian motorway fuel.
Be at the gate 45 minutes before. Passport for everyone, including the baby.
About 2 h. Eat on board, let the children run on deck, put the baby down in the buggy. Arrive Tallinn around 18:30.
Drop the car, walk to the market. Three floors of cheap food, a bakery, a supermarket. Everyone eats something different for €32.
Ten minutes' walk to the town hall square. Lit walls, empty streets, no crowds in November. The best free hour of the whole return.

alts: **Ferry timings vary by date** — Saturday sailings are roughly 07:30, 10:30, 13:30, 16:30 and 19:30, but confirm when you book and build the day around the actual departure.
**Skip Heureka to save €78?** Take the 13:30 ferry and spend the afternoon in Tallinn instead. The Old Town and Lennusadam are free/cheap.
note: Book the return ferry in the same session as the outbound — car space on winter Saturdays is limited and the cheap fares go first.

title: Tallinn → Vilnius, the last 600 km

callout.html: **Leave Tallinn by 10:00.** 600 km, seven hours of driving, and darkness from 16:15. Every hour you delay is an hour of night driving with three tired children.

items.p: Coffee, the town hall square, the walls. Thirty minutes, free, and the photographs are better than at midday.
Fuel at the ring road, snacks and water for the drive. This is the last leg.
128 km, 1 h 45. The children will sleep; do not stop unless you must.
Eight minutes off the main road. Sand, a playground, toilets, a thermos. The best leg-stretch on the route.
470 km, about 5 h 30 with two short stops. Cross into Latvia at Ikla, into Lithuania at Grenctāle.
Unload, bath, bed. Nobody cooks.

alts: **Want the submarine?** [[lennusadam]] opens at 10:00 on Sunday and takes two hours — but then you drive in the dark and reach Vilnius around 21:00. Only if the adults can share the driving.
**Break the drive:** stop at [[sigulda]] (1 h from Riga) or [[rundale]] — but only if you have a spare night.
note: Winter tyres are mandatory in Lithuania from 10 November and in Finland from 1 December — you are just inside the window, but check the tread before you go.
